suggestions.assertion: Identifies 'Claude in Excel' as Defect 6 (terminology) since this is Ch18, not Ch17
suggestions.reason: The expectation conflates two things: (1) identifying it as a terminology defect, and (2) numbering it as 'Defect 6'. The report uses its own issue numbering (Issue 1) but maps it to the 6th row in the taxonomy checklist. Consider splitting into 'identifies terminology violations' and 'maps to the correct defect category in the taxonomy' for clearer signal.

No expectation checks whether the report correctly distinguishes legitimate Ch 17 cross-references from incorrect Ch 18 terminology. The without_skill run correctly identified line 70 as a valid cross-reference — this discrimination is a quality signal worth asserting on, since a naive 'find and replace' approach would flag all instances incorrectly.

eval_feedback.overall: The expectations are well-designed and discriminating for this eval case. The without_skill baseline performs surprisingly well here — it passes all 5 expectations, which raises the question of whether this eval case can distinguish skill-vs-no-skill performance. Consider adding expectations around the specific defect taxonomy labels or the precision of the recommendations to create more separation.
